summary: Session set harvester-data-classifier completed all 4 sessions (Final) and is the canonical data-classification + sanitization pipeline on the harvester. Session 1 shipped the v1.0 classification.json keystone schema (10-category taxonomy + 7-strategy MaskingStrategy + FK-authority allOf + privacy-invariant valueFormatPattern constraint). Session 2 shipped the AccessHarvester classify subcommand (OLE DB schema reader + DAO interop for AutoNumber/RowSource + heuristics engine with PII veto rule + Jet/ACE-compatible cardinality subquery + value-format detector with raw values never stored). Session 3 shipped tools/classification-editor.html — a single-file zero-install editor that loads/saves classification.json, enforces the FK-authority allOf constraint in the UI, and flags suspect notes for raw PII pasting. Session 4 shipped the AccessHarvester sanitize subcommand: a CSV-per-table output (decided at session start per the spec's FK-remap stop rule), a deterministic RemapRegistry that memoizes old-value -> new-value lookups keyed by referenced (table, column), a two-pass FkGraphBuilder that decides PK remap then forces every referencing FK into lockstep, an EffectiveCategoryResolver that honours humanOverride precedence, and the seven MaskingHandlers (preserve / mock-replace via FNV-seeded LCG / generalize for DOB+ZIP / redact constant / scrub-free-text Lorem placeholder / regenerate epoch+constant / remap-id via the registry). The FK consistency invariant (plan § 5) is validated by FkConsistencyInvariantTests across standard, self-referencing, and preserved-PK shapes. 685/685 pipeline unit tests pass including 46 new sanitization tests; 3/3 SanitizeCommandTests integration tests pass against HomeHealthCare.accdb (the [SkippableFact] uses a synthesized minimal classification targeting tlkpPlanStatuses to avoid xUnit parallelization races against ClassifyCommandTests). Session 4 cross-provider verification VERIFIED on R1 by gemini-pro after the configured gpt-5-4 verifier hit OpenAI 429 — the verifier-failure escalation ladder directed the fall-back, which succeeded with a substantive 10-concern prose analysis ($0.074 R1 + $0.003 next-set analysis). Total set routed cost ~$2.13 across the four sessions. Phase 4 (SQL Server migration generator) from the data-classification-plan is explicitly deferred to a future session set per the spec's Out-of-scope clause.
